purpose: Authenticate users; manage session lifecycle; lock accounts after repeated failed attempts.

brief.text: Auth owns exactly three things: who is signed in, for how long, and when to stop letting someone try. Everything here is a consequence of one of those, and anything that is not one of them (passwords resets, machine identities, a second factor) is deliberately somewhere else — see Scope.
brief.how_it_fits: A **Session** is the unit of "signed in", and an **Account** is the unit of "allowed to try". They move independently: a session expires on its own clock (REQ-004), while an account locks on a counter that only failed logins touch (REQ-003). The pair meets in one place — a locked account may hold no active session — which is INV-002, and it is the invariant most of the other rules exist to keep true.
brief.why_this_way: Lockout counts attempts rather than rate-limiting time because the threshold has to be reviewable as a number (CON-001 = 5) rather than argued about as a policy. One active session per user (INV-001) is a deliberate narrowing: multi-device was cheaper to add later than to remove once anything depended on it.
brief.watch_out_for: The counter and the lock are two facts, not one, and REQ-003 is the only thing that keeps them consistent — read it before changing either. Q-003 is open on what a failed login against an already-locked account should do, so the Locked row of the matrix is a triaged gap rather than a settled answer.

entities.name: Session
entities.description: A logged-in instance of a User.

entities.name: Account
entities.description: Lockout state derived from failed attempts.

requirements.description: When a registered user submits valid credentials, the system shall create an Active session owned by that user.

ears.trigger: a registered user submits valid credentials
ears.response: create an Active session owned by that user

delta.note: The session must not have existed before the call — otherwise 'some Active session exists' is satisfied by one an earlier login created.

requirements.description: While a user's session is Active, when the user requests logout, the system shall transition that session to LoggedOut.

delta.note: Logging out something already logged out proves nothing.

requirements.description: If a login attempt fails while the account is Unlocked, then the system shall increment failedAttempts and lock the account when it reaches MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS.

ears.response: increment failedAttempts and lock the account when it reaches MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS

delta.note: The account must have been unlocked before the failure that locked it — a state where it was already Locked witnesses nothing about the lockout rule.

requirements.description: While a session is Active and has been inactive for longer than MAX_SESSION_AGE, the system shall transition it to Expired.

ears.state: the session is Active and has been inactive for longer than MAX_SESSION_AGE

delta.note: Only an Active session can expire.

requirements.description: While the account is Locked, if the user submits valid credentials, then the system shall refuse the login.

ears.response: refuse the login and leave every session and counter untouched

witness.justification: A prohibition has no reachable state to witness — there is no step in which 'the login did not happen' becomes visible. INV-002 (noSessionWhileLocked) carries the model-side proof.

invariants.description: At most one Active session per user.
A Locked account has no Active session.
Expired/LoggedOut sessions never appear in any user's active set.
Below MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS, the account stays unlocked.

constraints.name: MAX_SESSION_AGE
constraints.description: Modeled as a step counter for bounded checking.

states.name: Active
states.description: Session is live and accepted by the server.

states.name: Locked
states.description: Locked due to repeated failed login attempts. Not terminal — recoverable via unlock_account.

decisions.title: JWT (RS256) over session cookies
decisions.context: Edge proxy needs to validate tokens without a round-trip to the auth service.
decisions.decision: Use JWT signed with RS256 for session tokens.
decisions.rationale: Asymmetric signing lets the edge verify with the public key; private key stays in the auth service.

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Edge can't validate without a network hop.
Extra request per call adds latency and ops cost.

open_questions.question: Should unlock_account be available to a self-service flow (e.g. password reset) or only to Admin?
Session expiration: is it strictly time-based (inactivity timeout), or also bounded by absolute session age?

State×event gap: when Account=Locked and login_failed fires, the spec is silent (REQ-003 covers Unlocked only). Should attempts against a locked account be counted toward anything, ignored, or raise an alert?
